title: How Fix the Wi-Fi Connection Problem on Your Android Phone
excerpt: How Fix the Wi-Fi Connection Problem on Your Android Phone

body.text: Sunday, May 14, 2023

Everyone with a smartphone knows about Wifi. If nothing else, you know it’s what happens when you get your phone connected with a Wifi network you see a substantial change in the speed of your internet, the reason is the Wifi connection you got connected with is faster than the connection you have on your sim card. Do you know what does it take to connect your phone with a Wifi network and give you substantial browsing speed? There is a lot going on to make that connection go on. While we’re not going to discuss everything in detail and technical like the software stack or the radio interface hardware, but we are going to talk about the things as users we should know. Don’t worry, this’ll be fun, and of course a little more familiar with the android device you are using ! What is Wifi? Wifi refers to any local access wireless network that is based on the IEEE (Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers) 802.11 standards. Devices on a Wifi network transfer data through the airwaves using either a 2.4 GHz Ultra high frequency or 5 GHz Super high frequency. A Wifi setup comprises an Internet gateway (generally a modem) and an access point (router). The modem is connected to the Internet (a LAN connection), and the access point has a devoted connection to the modem. What the access point does is, filter the things you send and receive from the Internet and dispense them wirelessly to the android device or any other device connected with the Wifi and made the request. Why do I see so many available Wifi connections on my phone? When you start the Wifi on your phone, you see a list of every access point you’ve ever connected to, as well as every access point in range that broadcasts its presence. This can be a bit confusing for the reason that the an open network you connected to in Delhi in a Café Coffee Day will be listed, but you’re not likely going to be able to connect if you’re in hyderabad. It gets even more confusing when access points are named MGMT512 instead of “Mumbai Management Institute.” If you tap the scan button on your phone it will show you which access points are in range (and how strong the signal is based on the little icon) and which ones you have saved but are out of range. You can also delete old connections that you never want to use again just with a long tap on the connection name and then tapping on “Forget”. When you setup a Wifi network you have option to decide if the name of your Wi-Fi is broadcast and visible or not. If the SSID is not broadcast, it won’t be visible in your list and you’ll have to setup a connection yourself. Basic Wifi terminology (what do all those letters and numbers mean?) Like anything that can get a little technical, when you’re talking about Wi-fi networks you’re going to run into a lot of letters that stand for something in terms of Wi-Fi, for example: 11 a/b/g/n/ac:802.11 denotes to the IEEE (Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers) 802.11 specifications for wireless networking on the 2.4 GHz, 3.6 GHz, 5 GHz and 60 GHz frequencies. Any gadget that’s Wi-fi certified will follow these standards. The letter you see after 802.11 stands for a particular protocol that defines things like range and speed. Normally speaking, the “higher” the letter, the better is the potential range and speed of that connection. If you’ve bought a newer phone, it probably supports at least 802.11 n, and possible 802.11 ac. Most of the modern access points support them, too. Wi-fi: A trademarked term for a piece of wireless LAN instrument that supports the IEEE 802.11 arrangement. It’s a play on Hi-Fi, a term that stands for high fidelity and was popular for audio systems used years ago. If you see the word Wifi or WiFi or Wi-Fi on anything, that means it meets the standards and will work with other device that contains the Wi-fi trademarked name. Believe it or not, there are fakes out there that don’t meet things like transmission power necessities. Access point: An access point (when in terms of Wi-fi) is a device that allows other Wi-fi devices to connect to a wireless network. It can be an outside device, or it can be compacted into one piece of machine with a router, or even have a modem added to it. SSID: The service set identifier. It’s a human-readable string that can be up to 32 bytes long, and used as the network name you see in the list of Wi-fi access points on your phone when you search for the available wi-fi spots. MAC address: Short for Media Access Control address, is a unique identifier allotted to any networking gear by the manufacturer. While a MAC address is assigned to the hardware and is permanent by nature. WPS: Wi-fi Protected Setup is a security standard designed to help individual users having a secure wireless network without actually poking their nose into more technical things to adjust everything manually. Wifi Direct: A way of getting one Android device to talk to another using Wi-fi, but avoiding having to go through an Access Point. Secured Wi-fi vs. unsecured Wi-fi: Secured Wi-Fi are those networks which require you to enter a password to access through, on the other hand unsecured Wi-fi are those open networks which any one can connect and use while in the range. Open or unsecured Wi-Fi networks are more vulnerable in terms of security and anybody can use it illegally. You probably want to secure your Wifi network at home. That means you set up an encrypted password on your access point, and any and every device that wants to connect has to enter the same password for access. The security algorithm used for these connections may be WEP (Wired Equivalent Privacy), WPA (Wifi Protected Access) or WPA2 (a second generation and more secure version of WPA). Like everything else in the IEEE 802.11 specifications, security algorithms get revamped and improved. When security vulnerabilities were found in the WEP protocol, WPA was designed as a quick patch that all devices able to use WEP could also use. WPA2 came later, and is more secure, but some very old equipment may not support it. Andorid phones supports WPA2 and 802.1xEAP, and that’s the suggested way to secure any Wi-fi network. If you’re setting up a Wifi network yourself, you’ll want to get into a little more detail of the different security protocols and algorithms available, using WPA2 with a strong AES encrypted key is considered as safe until a professional hacker is after getting into your network. What is WPS? WPS stands for Wifi Protected Setup. The WPS allows users who don’t know a lot about wireless security to let their hardware set up automatically. When it works, it’s very easy and as secure as setup by a professional networking professional. The only problem with getting through it is that different manufacturers have different ways of starting WPS, and it’s a little clunky. There are four main methods to use WPS to add a device to a network — the PIN method, the push-button method, the NFC method and the USB method. NFC and USB are optional ways to set things up, however, Android devices generally use the Push Button or PIN method techniques, but in theory could support NFC and USB as well. To use WPS, it should be enabled on the router you want to connect to. Most Android users will then push a button on their router, then tap the WPS Push Button from the menu in the Wifi settings of their phones. Otherwise, you can connect to your routers control panel interface and use the PIN method. The Advanced Wifi Setup Menu on Android: If you want connect to a wireless network that doesn’t broadcast it’s SSID or needs special settings you will have to manually add a connection. There’s nothing complicated in here, but in order to connect to a SSID that’s hidden, you just enter the name of the network and choose the type of security it’s using. The rest goes the same way as connecting to a network that’s not hidden. Under the advanced options setting you will find two new options: Proxy settings and IP settings. On Android, you should know the Proxy Hostname and port to setup a connection that uses one. It might also happen that the router you’re connecting to may have a DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) server that assigns all the needed network info automatically when you are trying to connect to the this network, but, if it doesn’t, you’ll have to enter the information manually. While you’ll hardly ever need to set your IP address settings manually, there’s nothing wrong with knowing a few more things beforehand. Let’s discuss it further. IP address: This is the IP (Internet Protocol) address you want your Android to use. It has to be in the right network range (private IPv4 networks in general use 10.0.0.X, 172.16.0.X, or 192.168.X.X) and use an available number. Gateway: This is the IP address of a network node that acts can act as a router or proxy server both on the internal portion of the network as well as connecting it to the Internet in general. When you type http://www.jetking.cominto your browser, by default the request goes to the gateway which then directs the IP traffic so that the jetking website appears in your browser window. Network prefix length: This is the same thing as the subnet mask — a way to ensure that all devices on the network have the same network prefix. DNS: These are labeled 1 and 2. DNS is the Internet’s phone book. DNS servers translate a URL that we can read, into an IP address that computers can read more effortlessly. There are various options you can use here if you like. Once you have everything filled in right into the advanced settings menu of your phone’s wifi settings, press the connect button and you’ll be able to sign in and be using that Wifi network. The advanced Wifi settings menu This is one of those things that is very different from device to device. We’ll take a look at the settings and options you’re most likely to see here, and discuss them one by one so we all know what they mean. Wi-fi notifications: If you want to see a notification telling you there is a Wi-fi network available, you need this to be enabled. Internet availability: A setting using these words as a rule means that the Wi-fi network must have access to the Internet before your Android phone will connect to it. If this is disabled, you can connect to Wi-fi networks that do not have an active Internet connection. List sorting: Here you can choose to see your Wi-fi network list by availability and signal strength or alphabetically. Keep Wi-fi on when screen is off: This does unerringly what it says it does, but the significant part is knowing why you would want it enabled or disabled. If you set Wi-fi to shut off when the screen goes off, your phone have to use the cellular connection for any syncing or push messages. This incurs data charges of course. This uses more battery than Wi-fi. Normally, you want to keep Wi-fi on here. Allow Wi-fi scanning: This lets location services scan for active wireless access points to determine your phone’s location. Doing so can get your position quicker and draws less power than using GPS alone, but for the sake of privacy you can disable it here. Avoid poor connections: This switches you off of a Wi-fi network once the signal gets very feeble. It will either connect you to another Wi-fi network or back to 3G/4G network your data provider provides you when it stops the connection. Battery saving while on Wi-fi: This setting actually works! What it does is decelerate or stop your wireless radio’s network scanning. When your phone vigorously scans for available connections, it uses more power and your phone’s battery drains faster. The ability to change this setting is something that custom ROM builders have done since the G1, but now most vendors include it right in the advanced menu settings. If you disabled Wi-fi scanning for location, you might as well enable this and maximize every milliampere from your Android phone’s battery. Keep in mind, this isn’t meant to be course material for the TCP/IP portion of the MCSE exam, for that you need to read course books and probably some practical of live networks and servers. This is just a basic explanation to make you aware of everything you’re likely to come across at one time or another while using Wifi on your Android. While most of the time you can just enter a password and start using internet on your android phone, but, it’s always a good idea to have a little knowledge about everything you’re seeing and especially the technology you are using. Knowledge is power ! Suggestions and comments are always welcome, please free to feel share your thoughts in the box below.

However, it is complicated to have a positive attitude when life seems to be getting you down, but it isn’t impossible. Try finding the things that you are grateful for, doesn’t matter if they are small or seem insignificant, they should be able to offer you on the whole life satisfaction. When you nurture gratitude as part of your life, you can not only perk up your emotional sense of happiness, but also experience a superior sense of contentment. 10. Do things that Make You Happy: Take out time to do those things that make you really happy. Grab some dinner with a friend, watch a movie, play with your kids, read a book, go cycling, take a long walk with your loved ones or go shopping, do whatever you want to do to make yourself happy. When you are happy, your mood is always good and stress, anxiety, anger all these things seems like a million miles away. body.text: Monday, May 27, 2024

Introduction: In today's digital age, businesses face a constant barrage of cyber threats. Hackers are becoming more sophisticated, and their attacks can be quite harmful. But there's a silver lining: ethical hackers. These cybersecurity heroes use their skills to protect businesses from malicious attacks. Let's dive into the art of ethical hacking and learn how it can help safeguard your business. What is Hacking with an Ethic? Hacking with a lawful intent to evaluate a company's security is called ethical hacking, sometimes referred to as penetration testing or white-hat hacking. Ethical hackers stick to a code of ethics and get authorization before performing testing, their goal is to identify vulnerabilities before the bad guys do. Why Ethical Hacking is Crucial for Your Business? 1.Identify your weaknesses All businesses, no matter how big or little, have weaknesses. These could be insecure networks, out-of-date software, or weak passwords. Ethical hackers use realistic attack simulations to find these vulnerabilities. By identifying and addressing vulnerabilities, businesses can strengthen their defenses and lower the possibility of a breach. 2. Avoid Data Breach Incidents Data breaches may have disastrous consequences. They may result in monetary losses, legal issues, and reputational harm. Ethical hackers uncover and close security flaws to help prevent data leaks. By taking preventative measures, businesses can avoid the consequences of a cyberattack. 3. Stick to Rules There are strict regulations governing data security in many different businesses. Businesses can better adhere to these requirements by using ethical hacking to make sure their security procedures are up to date. It's critical to follow these guidelines as failing to do so may result in expensive penalties and other effects. The Process for Ethical Hacking 1. Identifying Information collection, or monitoring, is the initial stage in ethical hacking. Ethical hackers try to learn as much as they can about their targets. This could involve looking for software versions, scanning for open ports, and even looking through the social media accounts of staff members. Understanding the target's surroundings and locating possible access points are the objectives. 2. Examining Ethical hackers employ specialized tools to scan for vulnerabilities after they have sufficient knowledge. In this step, the target's systems are aggressively examined to identify flaws that could be misused. Commonly used scanning programs are OpenVAS, Nessus, and Nmap. 3. Getting access Ethical hackers look for weaknesses and try to take advantage of them to get access. This might entail using software defects, malicious code injection, or password cracking. The goal is to find out what information they can access and how far they can get inside the system. 4. Maintaining Access In real-world attacks, hackers often try to maintain access to a compromised system without being detected. Ethical hackers simulate this by installing backdoors or creating persistent access points. This step helps businesses understand how an attacker might remain undetected and continue to exploit their systems. 5. Taking Coverage of Tracks Covering tracks is the last stage. While ethical hackers use this to learn how an assault can go undetected, malicious hackers do this to evade detection. To do this, logs must be deleted, their presence must be concealed, and all traces of their actions must be eliminated. 6. Documentation Upon finishing their assessments, ethical hackers create an extensive report. The vulnerabilities they discovered, their methods of exploiting them, and suggestions for resolving the problems are all detailed in this study. It acts as a guide for companies looking to improve their security protocols. How to Implement Ethical Hacking in Your Business 1. Hire Skilled Ethical Hackers Bringing in the specialists is the first step. Hire penetration testing companies or certified ethical hackers (CEHs). These experts possess the knowledge and expertise to fully test your systems and offer useful insights. 2. Carry Out Frequent Security Audits Because cyber dangers continue to evolve, frequent security audits are necessary. Testing on a regular basis guarantee that newly discovered vulnerabilities are quickly found and fixed. Make ethical hacking a constant exercise instead of a one-time undertaking. 3. Educate Your Staff Security breaches are frequently caused by human error. Teach your staff the best practices for cybersecurity, which include protecting their devices, creating strong passwords, and identifying phishing emails. One of the most important lines of protection against cyberattacks is an informed workforce. 4. Put Strict Security Measures in Work Put in place strong security measures based on the information you learned from your ethical hacking attempts. This can involve fixing vulnerabilities, implementing multi-factor authentication, upgrading software, and improving network security. To remain ahead of possible risks, review and update these procedures regularly. 5. Develop an Incident Response Plan Even with the best of intentions, a breach could still happen. Have an emergency response plan in place and be ready. The actions to be taken in the event of a cyberattack, such as how to assess the damage, communicate with stakeholders, and control the breach, should be outlined in this strategy. A well-thought-out plan may reduce the effects of an attack and improve recovery. Curious to know more about ethical hacking and cyber security? Check out our blogs on our website. title: Quick Cybersecurity Habits You Need.
excerpt: In our digital age, the internet is vital for daily tasks, yet it poses risks. Cybersecurity is key for protecting personal data.

body.text: Monday, May 27, 2024

Introduction: In today's digital age, the internet is an integral part of our lives. From online banking to social media, we rely heavily on digital platforms for various activities. However, this convenience comes with risks. Cybersecurity is essential to protect our personal information and ensure our online safety. In this blog, we'll explore what cybersecurity is, and provide a set of quick habits to help you stay secure online. Cybersecurity: What is it? Cybersecurity is the discipline of protecting programs, networks, and systems from online threats. These cyberattacks frequently seek to extort money from users, access, alter, or destroy sensitive data, or interfere with regular business activities. There are more devices than people, making it difficult to implement efficient cybersecurity safeguards, and attackers are getting more creative. Fun Fact: The most common password is still "123456", followed closely by "password". Weak passwords are a major security risk. Why Is Cybersecurity Necessary? ​ Cybersecurity is essential for safeguarding sensitive data and preventing illegal access to financial and personal information. It ensures the confidentiality of private conversations and actions, helps individuals and businesses avoid costly data breaches, and sustains trust by protecting an organization's brand and customer relationships. Additionally, strong cybersecurity defenses prevent service interruptions and operational disruptions. Quick Cybersecurity Habits You Need! 1. Use Strong, Unique Passwords The first layer of protection against online attacks is a strong password. Make sure each account has a strong, distinct password. A mix of capital and lowercase letters, digits, and special characters make up a strong password. Think about utilizing a password manager to safely keep track of your passwords. 2. Enable two-factor verification (2FA) ​ Two-factor authentication strengthens the security of your accounts by demanding an additional form of verification in addition to your password. This can be an email verification or a code that is texted to your phone. It is far more difficult for attackers to access your accounts when 2FA is enabled. 3. Watch Out for Phishing Schemes Phishing schemes include sending phony emails or messages that seem official. Their goal is to steal private data, such bank account numbers or login credentials. Unwanted emails should be avoided, especially if they request private information. It is advisable to confirm the sender's identity before opening attachments or clicking on links. 4. Update your apps and software regularly Updating your software regularly is essential for safeguarding your devices from online attacks. Security patches are frequently included in software upgrades to address vulnerabilities. This holds for security software, apps, and operating systems. 5. Protect Your Wireless Network ​ Cybercriminals may target your home Wi-Fi network. Modify the router's default login information, and give your Wi-Fi network a strong, one-of-a-kind password. Make sure WPA3 or WPA2 encryption is in place on your network. 6. Make a data backup You may prevent data loss from hardware malfunctions or hackers by regularly backing up your data. Make use of automated backup programs and save copies of your files in several places, such the cloud and an external hard drive. 7. Make use of secure connections Make sure the websites you visit while online utilize HTTPS, which denotes a secure connection. Your internet connection can also be encrypted by using a Virtual Private Network (VPN), which adds extra protection, particularly while using public Wi-Fi networks. 8. Limit Personal Information Sharing ​ Take care while sharing information online, especially on social media. Don't reveal private information such as your phone number, home address, or bank account details. You can manage who can view your posts and personal data by adjusting your privacy settings. 9. Educate Yourself and Stay Informed The field of cybersecurity is always changing. Participate in training programs, read blogs from reliable cybersecurity news sources, and stay up to date on the latest risks and best practices. Educating oneself and others can contribute to the development of a safer online community. title: Become a Cloud Computing Pro: Essential Tips.
excerpt: As companies increasingly rely on digital infrastructure, cloud computing is essential in modern IT. Cloud engineers drive this efficiency and innovation.

body.text: Monday, May 27, 2024

With companies depending more and more on digital infrastructure, cloud computing is becoming an essential part of contemporary IT ecosystems. Cloud engineers are leading this technological revolution in efficiency and innovation. However, what is the job of a cloud engineer and how can one enter the field? Let's find these queries and dig into essential tips to make you a pro at cloud computing. How Do You Become a Cloud Engineer? An IT specialist in charge of developing, putting into practice, and overseeing cloud infrastructure and services is known as a cloud engineer. To provide scalable, safe, and reasonably priced cloud solutions, they collaborate with cloud service providers such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform. Cloud engineer’s responsibilities are: • Developing cloud architecture - Creating infrastructure that satisfies an organization's requirements for networking, computation, storage, and security. • Migration and Deployment - Introducing new cloud-native apps or transferring current ones to the cloud. • Management and maintenance - this includes processing updates, keeping an eye on performance, and making sure the cloud environment functions properly. • Security - Putting policies in place to shield apps and data from online dangers. • Cost management - This process of maximizing cloud usage to cut expenses without sacrificing functionality. A cloud engineer: what is that? A cloud engineer blends expertise from several IT fields, such as systems administration, networking, and software development. They need to be well-versed in programming and scripting, comprehend cloud technologies and services, and be highly aware of networking principles and security procedures. Cloud engineer's abilities consist of: • Expertise in AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud is required for cloud service providers. • Proficiency in scripting languages such as Bash or PowerShell and programming languages such as Python, Java, or Ruby. • Better understanding of Subnets, VPNs, firewalls, and virtual networks • Knowledge of orchestration tools (Kubernetes), containerization (Docker), and CI/CD pipelines. How to Work in Cloud Computing? To become a cloud engineer, take the following actions: • Education: A good starting point is a bachelor's degree in computer science, information technology, or a similar domain. • Certification: Azure Solutions Architect, and Google Cloud Professional Cloud Architect certifications are among the cloud providers that can speak to your abilities and enhance your employment opportunities. • Practical Experience: Getting real-world experience through internships, personal initiatives, or open-source project contributions is essential. • Constant Learning: Since cloud technology is always changing, it's important to keep up with webinars, online courses, and industry news. • Networking: Make connections with other cloud experts by attending conferences, joining professional groups, and attending events. Essential Tips for Becoming a Pro in Cloud Computing Master the Basics: Make sure you have a solid grasp of basic ideas like networking, storage, and virtualization. Learn about the various cloud deployment options (public, private, hybrid) and service models (IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS). Get Certified: In the industry, cloud certifications are highly regarded. Gradually move up to more specialized certificates after earning entry-level ones. Certifications show prospective employers your expertise and dedication. Practical Application: Theory alone is insufficient. Utilize the free tiers that cloud providers give to set up your cloud environment. Practice configuring services, deploying apps, and resource management. Learn DevOps and Automation: Effective cloud management relies on automation. Learn about CI/CD tools like Jenkins, configuration management tools like Ansible, and infrastructure as code (IaC) tools like Terraform. Managing cloud infrastructure will become easier for you if you grasp the DevOps principles. Keep Security in Mind: Cloud security is important. Study up on network security, encryption, identity and access management (IAM), and compliance standards. Keep up with new developments in your field to stay ahead of any challenges. Know Cost Management: Improper management of cloud expenses can cause them to increase costs. To prevent needless spending, get proficient with the cost management tools offered by cloud providers and work on optimizing resource consumption. Stay up to date: To keep your skills up to date, take advanced classes, attend webinars, and read blogs written by industry professionals. For some important resources check out our blogs Join Communities: Participate in online forums related to cloud computing on sites like Stack Overflow, Reddit, and GitHub. Peer networking can provide perspectives, encouragement, and collaborative opportunities. Develop Soft Skills: For a cloud engineer, teamwork, communication, and problem-solving abilities are essential. It's common to collaborate with cross-functional teams and must clarify complex concepts to stakeholders who lack technical expertise. Create a Portfolio: Use a professional portfolio to highlight your accomplishments and abilities. Provide case studies of cloud solutions you've used to demonstrate your technical proficiency and problem-solving skills. Don't just dream about becoming a cloud computing pro. title: Cyber Security A Complete Guide
excerpt: Stay secure in the digital age with our guide. Protect against ransomware, data breaches, and threats.

body.text: Saturday, June 01, 2024

Introduction: In the current digital era, the threat landscape is ever-changing. Cyber risks are rising as our reliance on technology grows. Ransomware attacks, data breaches, and other cyberthreats are growing in frequency and sophistication. Strong cybersecurity measures are more important than ever as people and organizations become more interconnected. Comprehending the fundamentals of cybersecurity is essential to safeguarding confidential data and preserving system integrity. This guide intends to make cybersecurity ideas understandable and offers practical ways to protect what you do online. Fun Fact: The cybersecurity industry has a zero percent unemployment rate! What is Cybersecurity? The process of protecting networks, systems, and data from online threats that aim to steal, corrupt, or interfere with data and services is known as cybersecurity. It includes a broad range of procedures and guidelines designed to guarantee the confidentiality, accessibility, and authenticity of data. Cybersecurity is now essential for preventing unwanted access, alteration, and destruction of sensitive data due to the growing number of internet-connected devices and the sophistication of cyber threats. It entails utilizing a range of instruments and methods, including intrusion detection systems, firewalls, encryption, and antivirus software, in addition to putting best practices like frequent updates, secure code, and user training into effect. Additionally, risk management and guaranteeing adherence to legal and regulatory standards are just as important aspects of cybersecurity as technology. In a Effective cybersecurity policies are crucial for protecting personal, business, and national security in an era where cyber threats are always changing. The CIA Triad The foundation of cybersecurity is built on the CIA Triad: Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability . These three principles are essential for ensuring a secure and reliable system. 1. Confidentiality: Ensures that sensitive information is accessed only by authorized individuals. Techniques such as encryption and access control are used to protect data from unauthorized access. 2. Integrity: Ensures that information is accurate and unaltered. This involves maintaining the consistency, accuracy, and trustworthiness of data over its lifecycle. Techniques include hashing and digital signatures. 3. Availability: Ensures that information and resources are accessible to authorized users when needed. This involves implementing proper maintenance, hardware repairs, and network bandwidth allocation to prevent outages and disruptions. Seven Major Types of Cyber Attacks Understanding the most common kinds of cyber-attacks may encourage enhanced awareness and measures. These are the top seven categories of cyberattacks: 1. Malware: Computer, server, or network harm inflicted by malicious software. Worms, trojans, and viruses are a few examples. Malware could change essential functions, steal, encrypt, or remove data, as well as track user behavior. 2. Phishing: A type of fraud in which fraudsters pose as reliable organizations or individuals via email or other correspondence. The goal of phishing attempts is to get private information, such as credit card numbers and login credentials. 3. Ransomware: Malware of this kind encrypts the files of its victims. After the victim pays the ransom, the attacker requests access to the data again. Ransomware assaults have increased significantly in recent years aimed at companies and government agencies. 4. Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) and Denial of Service (DoS) attacks seek to prevent authorized users from accessing a computer or network resource. DoS attacks usually entail sending an excessive number of requests to the computer or resource that is being attacked. DDoS assaults are initiated by several compromised systems. 5. Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) Attacks: These are attacks in which the attackers assume the role of a mediator between two parties and use their communication to intercept and maybe modify it. Due to this, financial data, login passwords, and personal information may be stolen. 6. SQL Injection: A hacker accesses data not meant to be seen by manipulating a backend database using malicious SQL code. Numerous sensitive data items, including user lists, private client information, and personal customer details, may be included in this. 7.Zero-Day Exploit: This type of attack targets a vulnerability that the target software manufacturer and other interested parties are unaware of and would like to fix. Zero-day exploits can be very damaging and difficult to prevent. In the fight against cyber threats, education and training play a pivotal role. Jetking’s Cyber Security Course is designed to equip you with the skills and knowledge needed to protect against cyber threats. The course covers a wide range of topics, including network security, ethical hacking, data encryption, and more. By enrolling in Jetking’s Cyber Security Course, you will learn : • Fundamentals of Cybersecurity: Understand the basic principles of cybersecurity and the CIA Triad. • Threat Detection and Prevention: Learn how to identify and mitigate various types of cyber threats. • Security Protocols and Technologies: Gain hands-on experience with the latest security tools and protocols. • Compliance and Legal Frameworks: Understand the importance of cybersecurity laws and regulations. • Real-World Applications: Work on real-world scenarios and case studies to apply your knowledge in practical settings. Jetking’s Cyber Security course offers comprehensive training that can help you build a strong foundation in cybersecurity. title: How to Become Masters in Cloud Computing
excerpt: Master Cloud Computing: Your guide to mastering cloud technology. From basics to advanced skills, excel in the dynamic field of cloud computing.

body.text: Saturday, June 01, 2024

Introduction: Hello and welcome to the exhilarating world of crazy learning! Today, with the help of these 10 dynamic steps, you’re about to embark on an exciting journey to master cloud computing. Get ready to dive into a whirlwind of knowledge and skills that will transform you into a cloud computing expert. So, fasten your seatbelt and let’s get into the cloud! Master Cloud Computing: Steps to Becoming an Expert In the world of modern technology, cloud computing stands as one of the most revolutionary advancements. It powers everything from our favorite streaming services to the seamless functioning of businesses globally. But how do you go from a curious beginner to a cloud computing expert? Let’s understand with the following steps. Step 1 Understand the basics of cloud computing A firm understanding of the foundations is necessary before going too far. Delivering computer services via the internet, or "the cloud," includes servers, storage, databases, networking, software, and more. The following are the fundamental ideas you should comprehend: • Types of Cloud Services: Familiarize yourself with Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), and Software as a Service (SaaS). • Deployment Models: Know the difference between public, private, and hybrid clouds. • Key Providers: Get to know the major players in the field, like Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP). Think of this stage as learning the alphabet before you start forming sentences. Step 2 Let’s dive deep into the cloud technology After establishing a strong base, it's time to investigate the cloud's underlying technologies. Start by familiarizing yourself with the two fundamental cloud computing technologies: virtualization and containerization. In this field, tools like Docker, Kubernetes, and VMware are essential. • Virtualization: Understand how virtual machines (VMs) work and how they enable multiple operating systems to run on a single physical server. • Containerization: Learn about containers, which allow applications to be packaged with their dependencies, ensuring they run consistently in any environment. Step 3 Get hands on experience on cloud technology platforms While theory is valuable, nothing compares to real-world experience. Open an account with AWS, Azure, or GCP on the free tier and begin testing. Construct your virtual servers, configure databases, and try launching apps. Jetking's cloud computing course offers industry-simulating laboratories and real-world projects that make it the ideal platform for gaining this practical experience. Step 4 Learn to automate cloud computing processes The cloud computing genie of automation makes processes error-free and efficient. Learn how to use Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools such as AWS CloudFormation and Terraform. Using these technologies, you may script your cloud architecture, which simplifies deployment and management. Step 5 master Cloud security Security in the cloud is critical. Discover the best practices for cloud security, like identity and access management (IAM), data encryption, and compliance requirements. Gaining expertise in cloud environment security will make you a priceless asset to any company. Step 6 explore advanced topics on cloud computing After you've mastered the fundamentals, begin studying more complex subjects like: • Discover serverless computing: which enables you to run code without setting up or maintaining servers, with services like AWS Lambda and Azure Functions. • large Data and Analytics: Recognize how analytics services are provided and how large data is handled via cloud platforms. • Learn about cloud-based machine learning and artificial intelligence services. Step 7 Get certified on cloud computing Certifications are a great way to validate your skills and stand out in the job market. Some highly regarded certifications include: • AWS Certified Solutions Architect • Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert • Google Professional Cloud Architect Jetking's cloud computing course is designed to help you prepare for these certifications, providing you with the knowledge and confidence to ace the exams. Step 8 stay updated on newer developments in cloud computing In the dynamic sector of cloud computing, new technologies and best practices are constantly being developed. Engage with industry blogs, seminars, and discussion boards such as Reddit and Stack Overflow. Making connections with other cloud experts can also help you stay current on developments and offer insightful information. Step 9 Build cloud applications and project portfolio Organize your projects into a portfolio to highlight your abilities. Possessing actual projects will make an impression on prospective employers and clients, whether it's a personal blog hosted on AWS, a serverless application utilizing Azure Functions, or a data analytics project on GCP. Step 10: Continuous Learning and Networking Cloud computing is a journey rather than a destination. Improve your talents constantly by attending conferences, workshops, and advanced courses. Getting involved in industry events and joining professional associations can open doors to networking that could lead to your next big career move. title: Why upskilling in cloud computing is a must for Indian Profe
excerpt: Upskilling in cloud computing is crucial for Indian professionals due to high demand and skill gaps. It enhances productivity and career growth.

body.text: Thursday, July 25, 2024

Introduction Cloud computing has become a key tool in today's quickly changing digital landscape, transforming industries and spurring innovation. Upskilling in cloud computing is not only advantageous for Indian workers but also essential. These are the main causes for this. Growing need for expertise in the cloud Numerous industries are experiencing a sharp increase in demand for cloud computing knowledge. Cloud technology plays a crucial role in enabling agility, scalability, and creativity in digital transformation activities, which are commonly prioritized by enterprises. Businesses understand they need specialized workers like cloud developers, administrators, and security specialists to remain competitive. The increased demand serves as a reminder of how important cloud computing is in contemporary workplaces. Bridging the Skill Gap The labor market still has a sizable skills gap even if the demand for cloud knowledge is rising. Upskilling is crucial since there is a significant gap between the supply and demand of cloud workers. Around 2 million cloud specialists will be needed in India by 2025, according to predictions, to fulfill the growing demand in industries like IT, finance, and healthcare. To provide the existing workforce with the skills it needs to close this gap, an upskilling initiative is essential. Improving opportunities for a cloud computing career Developing one’s skills in cloud computing not only meets industry demands but also greatly improves one’s professional opportunities. Experts in the cloud are more in demand by businesses and frequently fetch more compensation. More training in this area may result in promotions and greater work chances given the increasing emphasis on cloud-based solutions. Proficiency in cloud computing is an advantageous trait for individuals seeking to progress in their professions. Efficiency in operation and forward-looking. Cloud technologies increase productivity and save expenses, which leads to an improvement in operational efficiency. Experts in cloud computing can optimize processes, offering significant advantages as companies grow. Additionally, keeping up with the latest technological developments through upskilling enables workers to future-proof their professionals. Following the most recent developments in cloud computing guarantees their continued relevance in a constantly evolving work environment. Impact of the Pandemic The COVID-19 epidemic increased the shift to remote work and led to a considerable increase in the use of cloud computing services. Businesses made significant investments in cloud technologies to sustain operations and productivity during lockdowns. Professionals with expertise in cloud services and digital tools are becoming more and more in demand as this trend continues. To fulfill the new operational demands defined by the pandemic's effects on the workplace, cloud computing upskilling is essential. An initiative from the Government and businesses Proposals from the government, such as the Digital India Program, support professional development in digital technologies, particularly cloud computing. The objectives of these initiatives are to boost economic growth and operational efficiency. In addition, as businesses adjust to the digital transition, many are placing high priority on employee training. This highlights the significance of cloud computing skills in the contemporary job market and underlines the urgent need for upskilling across the workforce. Conclusion For professionals in India, they must upgrade their skills in cloud computing. Proficiency in cloud computing is vital due to several factors, including growing demand, a notable skills shortage, greater job opportunities, increased operational efficiency, the pandemic's effects, and encouraging government and business activities. Professionals can make sure they are competitive and relevant in a quickly changing digital world by investing in cloud skills. body.text: Saturday, October 05, 2024

Introduction Hardware networking is the most in-demand skill in terms of infrastructure, from simple personal devices to vast global infrastructures, in the lightning-speed digital world today. This blog will take you through a step-by-step journey in a very rewarding career in hardware networking. Step 1: Get a Good Base in Hardware Networking Fundamentals A good foundation for building a network means that one needs to start by learning the more complex aspects of hardware networking. Hardware Networking is concerned with the basic, physical infrastructure that connects computers, servers, and other devices in such a manner that they may efficiently communicate with one another. This includes routers, switches, cables, and all devices that make networks function efficiently. Key concepts to grasp include: - Types of networks (LAN, WAN, MAN) - Network protocols (e.g., TCP/IP, DHCP, DNS) - Network topologies and configurations Courses in basic networking or entry-level certifications like CompTIA Network+ can lay the necessary foundation. Jetking's BCA program (Bachelor of Computer Applications) provides a solid grounding with exposure to all basic IT fundamentals besides an overall introduction to networking. Know more about Jetking's BCA program. This will provide the much-needed foundation to stand strong in hardware networking, having been drafted according to the current industry demand. Step 2: Obtain Core Networking Certifications Not only do certifications validate your skills and make you stand apart in an already competitive job market, but they are also very integral to the hardware networking process. Among some of the most recognized include: Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA): Know it to be one taken as a must in the industry, proving you know how to install, configure, and troubleshoot the networks. Major credential that employers look for. CompTIA Network+: Good starting point that covers foundational concepts of networking. Microsoft Certified: Windows Server Fundamentals: Glimpse into managing server infrastructure. Each of these certifications enhances your resume, signaling your competence in hardware networking. Step 3: Gain Practical Experience Theoretical knowledge will only take you so far. In a field like hardware networking, hands-on experience is key. Seek internships, entry-level jobs, or freelance opportunities where you can work on actual networking tasks, such as setting up routers, switches, and firewalls, troubleshooting network issues, and performing regular network maintenance. Jetking’s practical lab sessions simulate real-world scenarios, helping students build confidence in working with networking equipment and solving problems in real-time. Step 4: Specialize in an Area of Interest It can be a really broad field of hardware networking; hence, specialization is what can better sharpen focus and deepen expertise. Some of the sought-after specializations include the following: Network Security: This is one of the critical specializations since cyber threats have also become a common phenomenon. The focus of this particular area is on maintaining the security of data and ensuring that the network sounds. Specializing is what refines your skills, and above all, enhances your marketability, thus making you more attractive to employers. The influx of AI, Cloud Computing, 5G, and IoT is changing the domain of networking in a way that demands new skill sets to navigate through such advancements. body.text: Monday, October 07, 2024

The rise of AI has revolutionized the way we create visual content. In 2024, both individuals and businesses are increasingly turning to AI tools for producing stunning images and videos with minimal effort. Whether you are a content creator, a marketer, or simply someone looking to enhance your digital presence, there are numerous free AI tools available that can help streamline your creative process. Below, we explore the top 10 best free AI tools for video and image creation in 2024. 1. Canva Best For: Beginners and professional marketers Platform: Web, iOS, Android Canva is a widely popular platform for designing visual content, and its AI-powered features make it even better in 2024. With the integration of AI design tools like Magic Resize and Background Remover, Canva enables users to create high-quality images and videos effortlessly. Its drag-and-drop interface and pre-made templates allow even beginners to design professional visuals in minutes. Moreover, Canva’s free version provides an impressive range of stock photos, videos, and design elements. Key Features: AI-based background remover Magic Resize for adapting designs to different dimensions Extensive library of templates, images, and videos Collaborative tools for teams 2. Runway ML Best For: Advanced video creation and VFX Platform: Web Runway ML is an advanced AI tool designed for video creators who want to add unique visual effects and manipulate content with AI-driven precision. In 2024, Runway ML is equipped with powerful features like video inpainting (removing unwanted elements from video) and AI-generated video effects. Its intuitive interface allows you to use complex machine learning models without any technical expertise. Key Features: Real-time video editing and effect generation Background removal in video content AI-powered video inpainting and object replacement Accessible for non-technical users Read this also: Top 10 Best Low-Budget Laptops for Hacking in 2024 3. DALL·E 3 Best For: Generating artistic images Platform: Web DALL·E 3, developed by OpenAI, is a game-changing AI tool that generates images based on text prompts. It stands out for creating imaginative and creative artwork, making it perfect for content creators, designers, and artists. As of 2024, DALL·E 3 offers improved image quality, consistency, and realism compared to its predecessors. Its unique ability to interpret complex text prompts into images allows users to visualize their ideas in ways they never could before. Key Features: Text-to-image generation based on detailed prompts High-quality, realistic images Enhanced control over artistic styles and compositions 4. Pictory Best For: Turning text into videos Platform: Web Pictory is a fantastic AI tool for transforming long-form text content into engaging videos, making it a favorite among content marketers and bloggers in 2024. By simply uploading your article or blog post, Pictory creates a video summary with visuals, transitions, and voiceovers. It’s ideal for turning written content into visually appealing marketing assets or social media videos. Key Features: AI-driven video creation from text content Automatic selection of relevant video clips and images Built-in voiceover feature Customizable video templates 5. Lumen5 Best For: Social media video creation Platform: Web Lumen5 continues to be one of the go-to AI video creation tools in 2024. Its AI engine analyzes text and automatically suggests visuals, music, and transitions to turn content into engaging videos. Lumen5 is perfect for social media managers and marketers looking to create videos that are tailor-made for platforms like Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook. Key Features: AI-assisted video creation from blog posts or scripts Thousands of pre-designed video templates Easy social media integration Free tier offers ample functionality for basic video creation 6. Deep Dream Generator Best For: AI art and style transfer Platform: Web Deep Dream Generator is a unique AI tool that generates dreamlike, surreal images by applying artistic styles to your existing photos. In 2024, it remains a favorite for artists and creators looking to explore AI-assisted creativity. The platform uses neural networks to analyze and enhance images in visually stunning ways, making it perfect for artistic projects. Key Features: AI-based artistic style transfer Large selection of filters and effects Easy-to-use interface for creating unique, artistic visuals Free version with high-quality output options 7. HitPaw Video Enhancer Best For: Enhancing low-resolution videos Platform: Web HitPaw Video Enhancer is an AI-driven tool that enhances video quality by upscaling low-resolution content and improving clarity. In 2024, it’s widely used by video editors and marketers to enhance the quality of their videos without needing advanced editing skills. The AI upscaling feature automatically adjusts video resolution, making blurry videos crisp and clear. Key Features: AI-based video upscaling Noise reduction and clarity improvement One-click enhancement process Free trial version available with basic features 8. Artbreeder Best For: Generating and mixing images Platform: Web Artbreeder is a creative AI platform that enables users to generate images by mixing and modifying existing ones. In 2024, it remains a popular choice for artists, designers, and game developers. The platform uses machine learning to combine images and create new, unique versions. Whether you need character portraits, landscapes, or abstract designs, Artbreeder offers endless possibilities. Key Features: AI-based image blending and customization Creation of portraits, landscapes, and abstract art Simple interface for non-designers Free access to basic features and downloads 9. Designify Best For: Quick image background removal and editing Platform: Web Designify is an AI-powered tool that focuses on removing image backgrounds, making it an ideal tool for e-commerce, marketers, and designers in 2024. It automates the process of extracting objects from their backgrounds with pixel-perfect precision, allowing users to place them on different scenes or use them in promotional material. Key Features: Instant background removal High-resolution downloads Free to use with basic editing features Ideal for creating transparent PNG images 10. Kapwing Best For: Collaborative video editing Platform: Web Kapwing is a web-based AI tool that offers a variety of video editing features and collaborative tools. It is widely used by teams for creating marketing videos, tutorials, and social media content. In 2024, Kapwing remains one of the best free tools due to its seamless integration of AI and editing capabilities. Its AI-powered tools can automatically generate subtitles, resize videos for different platforms, and more. Key Features: AI-generated subtitles and translations Collaborative video editing workspace Easy-to-use timeline and editing tools Free tier with significant features Conclusion: ​In 2024, creating high-quality video and image content has never been easier, thanks to the rapid advancements in AI technology. Whether you are a professional content creator, a marketer, or a hobbyist, these top 10 free AI tools can help you create stunning visuals and videos with minimal effort. From AI-driven video generation to artistic style transfers, these tools provide endless possibilities for enhancing your creativity while saving time and resources. ​ To get more Information about Cloud Computing with AI courses Visit on our official site. ​ FAQs: ​ Are these tools completely free to use? Most of the tools listed offer free versions with basic features. However, some may require paid subscriptions for advanced functionalities. Do I need technical expertise to use AI for video and image creation? No, most of these tools are designed to be user-friendly and accessible even for beginners. Can I use these AI tools for commercial projects? Yes, many of these AI tools allow for commercial use, but it's always a good idea to check their specific licensing terms. What are the limitations of free AI tools? Free versions often come with limitations like watermarks, limited resolution, or restricted access to premium features. Paid versions may be necessary for more professional needs. How do I choose the right tool for my needs? ​Consider the type of content you're creating (e.g., social media videos, artistic images) and the tool’s ease of use, output quality, and features.

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS): Overview TCS is one of the IT services companies in India. Being a leading company, its portfolio covers a wide range of services. It works with database management and other sectors. TCS provides an enjoyable work environment promoting innovation and skills growth. Why TCS?: Extensive training programs are provided, competitive pay, and global projects. Suitable for freshers and even experienced. 2. title: How to Get a Cisco Networking Certification?
excerpt: Choose a Cisco certification track, study, practice hands-on, and take the exam via Pearson VUE. Recertify every 3 years through exams or credits.

body.text: Monday, October 14, 2024

Introduction In this rapidly changing IT world, a Cisco certification is highly valued by employers as it can validate that the professional possesses certain networking skills. Whether you work to become a network administrator, a systems engineer, or even a network architect, a Cisco certification can turn your life around. Here is how to get a Cisco Networking Certification easily. 1. Understand the Cisco Certification Levels Cisco is rather divided into several levels of certification for specific areas of interest: Entry Level: This includes the Cisco Certified Entry Networking Technician (CCENT), a great starting point for beginners who want to build foundational networking skills. Associate Level: The Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA) is one of the most popular certifications and covers broad topics like networking fundamentals, IP services, security fundamentals, and automation. Professional Level: The Cisco Certified Network Professional (CCNP) is ideal for individuals who want to specialize in more advanced areas, such as enterprise networking, security, data center, or wireless networks. Expert Level: Cisco Certified Internetwork Expert (CCIE) is the highest level and is targeted at professionals who want to master networking skills. 2. Choose the Appropriate Certification Programme There are several tracks through Cisco, and you can choose one that suits your career requirements the best. The most popular among them are as follows: Enterprise: This is helpful when you have solid thoughts of specializing in enterprise networking. CCNA Enterprise comes to your rescue-the prime focus is on understanding enterprise networks and the underlying processes that go with them. Security: If you have a deep interest in cybersecurity, the CCNP Security or CCIE Security tracks are for you. Data Center: For those dealing with data and cloud infrastructures, CCNP Data Center is the right choice. Collaboration: CCNP Collaboration will be suited best for people who deal with voice, video, and conferencing-related technologies in the telecommunication field. Choose either of the paths according to your current job profile or career ambitions. Also Read: Top 10 Companies Hiring Database Administrators in India 3. Fulfill any requirements Some Cisco certifications have prerequisites. For example: CCNA: No formal requirements, although having a minimal knowledge of networking is very helpful. CCNP: It needs a hold of either the CCNA or at least equivalent knowledge. Besides that, prerequisite professional-level exams must be passed. CCIE: The candidate requires deep knowledge in the domain of networking and passing both a written and a hands-on lab exam. Make sure you fulfill the prerequisites before applying for the exam. 4. Study the Official Cisco Curriculum Cisco provides official resources and study guides, which are the best place to start. They offer a range of materials: Cisco’s Official Study Guides: Available for each certification level. These cover exam topics in detail and provide practical exercises. Cisco Networking Academy: Offers courses and training modules that help you prepare for exams. You can choose self-paced learning or instructor-led courses. Official Certification Guides: Books tailored to Cisco exams, providing focused content on what you need to know. 5. Practice by Doing In theory, but also hands-on preparation before one takes on the Cisco certifications, preparing for one is key. How to get there: Set Up a Home Lab: With this, you will have the chance to practice real-world networking scenarios. This allows one to set up routers, switches, and virtual machines in replicating complex networks. Practice Simulations: With the likes of Packet Tracer for Cisco and GNS3, the opportunity to simulate networking environments and experiment with different configurations is possible without having actual hardware to work on. 6. Leverage Practice Exams and Dumps First, you have to prepare yourself by giving practice tests before scheduling an appointment for a test. Websites, such as Boson, ExamTopics, and Cisco Learning Network, offer various practice tests for Cisco certifications. Practice Dumps: These will give you an idea about the type of questions asked in the test and also prepare you for the type of question formats. Review Weak Areas: When you have taken enough practice tests, review all your weak areas and focus on enhancing your knowledge in those topics. 7. Report and Take the Exam Once you feel prepared, you can enroll to sit for the exam. Cisco exams are delivered by Pearson VUE, which is a third-party testing provider that is independent of Cisco. Here is how you do it: Create a Cisco Account: You go to the Cisco Certification website and create your account. Select Exam and Testing Center: You can take an exam at Pearson VUE Testing Center or you can opt for the online proctored exam if available for the concerned certification. Exam Day Preparation: On the day of your exam ensure you have all necessary documents and materials ready for identification purposes. Relax and have a good sleep. 8. Recertification Retention Cisco certifications last 3 years. After which you have to recertify if you still want to maintain your knowledge about the CCNA domain. Cisco does provide three options for recertification: Take a Recertification Exam: You need to pass the same or higher-level exam to renew the certification. Acquire Continuing Education Credits: You earn credits by attending the webinars, workshops, or courses approved by Cisco, which add up toward recertification. Achieve higher certification: Passing a higher-level certification, such as CCNP after CCNA, will automatically renew your existing, lower-level certification. Conclusion: A Cisco certification opportunity often leads to many careers in networking, systems management, and even cybersecurity. Follow a study plan then gain practical experience by using official Cisco materials which will keep you well-prepared to pass your certification exams. Read our blogs | Visit our courses ​

title: Free Photo Editing Apps for Social Media
excerpt: Enhance your social media with free editing apps like Snapseed, Canva, and VSCO—ideal for students creating standout posts with ease!

body.text: Monday, October 14, 2024

Introduction When it comes to enhancing your social media presence, photo editing plays a crucial role in making your images stand out. Fortunately, there are many free photo editing apps available that offer a wide range of tools to help you create visually appealing content without breaking the bank. Whether you're adjusting brightness, adding filters, or fine-tuning details, these apps make it easy for anyone to elevate their photos and capture their audience's attention. 1. Snapseed For Accurate Editing Why It's Great: Snapseed is a powerful photo editing tool developed by Google. It brings to you a professional suite of features through an easy-to-use user interface. With Snapseed, you can fine-tune your photos or apply creative effects. Key Features: - Filters: Snapseed offers a ton of filters from vintage to modern giving your shots that special look. - Editing tools: such as selective adjustments, healing brushes, and perspective correction for minute details. - Easy-to-use interface: Snapseed is a user-friendly image editing tool even for new users. Ideal For: Students who need to make detailed adjustments or apply artistic filters to their photos. It's particularly useful for those who want to enhance their academic or personal photos with professional-quality edits. 2. Adobe Photoshop Express: The Professional Touch Why It's Great: Adobe Photoshop Express gives users a flavor of the company's legendary Photoshop capabilities in mobile-friendly form. It is a great option for students who want to have advanced features at their fingertips but do not want to clutter the full Photoshop software. Key Features: - Basic photo adjustments are easily available that adjust brightness, contrast, and color balance. - One-Touch Filters: With a wide variety of preset filters, seamlessly improve your images. - Text and Collage Options: Add your text overlay and photo collage to enhance the engagement of your posts. Ideal For: Students seeking a blend of simplicity and advanced features for both personal and project-related photo edits. It’s also a great tool for creating visually appealing presentations. 3. Pixlr: Creative and Versatile Why It Great: What sets Pixlr apart is its combination of user-friendliness with more advanced editing features. It offers a whole set of tools for both new users and professional editors. Key Features: - Auto-Fix Feature: One touch to perfect, making quick fixes incredibly easy. - Filter and Overlay Variety: Choose from an almost endless selection of filters and effects in your images. - Collage Maker: Make gorgeous collages with amazing layouts and designs. Ideal For: To be used by students who would love to try creative effects and need flexible editing capabilities for fast edits as well as more specific ones. 4. Canva: Why It's Great: Design and Edit in an Easy Peasy Way in Canva. It is just not a photo editor; it is something more of a design and creation tool that makes professional quality social media posts, such as presentations. Its ease of use and a vast library make it a student favorite. Key Features: - Pre-designed templates for social media posts, stories, and presentations are available. - Simple Photo Editing Tools: Makes it simple to adjust brightness and contrast; and apply filters. - Graphics and Fonts: Graphics, icons, and fonts-just like all these are used for making your design look beautiful. Ideal for: Students who want to make their social media posts, stories, and presentations most attractive and appealing. The interface of Canva design is ideal for those active in campus clubs or extracurricular activities. 5. VSCO: Chic and Minimalistic Why It's Great: VSCO has extremely high-quality filters and a rather minimalist user interface. It is perfect for users who want near-perfectly polished, professional-looking photos that don't require much work from the user themselves. Key Features: - High-Quality Filters: Apply premium filters that give your photos a unique and sleek look. - Basic Editing Tools: Make minor changes to exposure, contrast, and sharpness. - Easy Navigation: This application has a pretty simple interface that leans towards good aesthetics for your images. Ideal For: These are suitable for students who like the clean aesthetic and need to create visually attractive images to snap in quick steps. It's also really good for people who love sharing their personal work or creative output in a shareable space, such as Instagram. 6. InShot: Photo and Video Editing for Anything Why it's great: InShot comes with an entire set of image and video editing features. This makes it a great option for students who need to curate and edit all their multimedia files. Key Features: - Photo and Video Editing: Trim, crop, and apply effects to photos and videos - Collage Maker: Make customized layouts using InShot's collage-making feature. - Add text stickers and emojis to personalize your content. Ideal For: It is best suited for students performing multimedia projects or who want to create engaging content with pictures and videos included. It is an ideal application to capture and share pictures of events or personal experiences happening in the college. Conclusion ​ If you're ready to take your editing skills to the next level and create professional-quality content, why not explore more advanced tools? title: How Can I Become a Networking Engineer in 2024?
excerpt: Become a networking engineer in 2024 by gaining a relevant degree, certifications, hands-on experience, and mastering tech like cloud computing and 5G.

body.text: Friday, October 18, 2024

Introduction A networking engineer designs, implements, and manages computer networks that support voice, data, video, and wireless services. They ensure the smooth, secure, and efficient operation of networking systems. In 2024, it is more imperative than ever that network automation, cloud computing, and 5G technology have a well-designed and powerful kind of workforce in the form of skilled networking engineers. Steps to Becoming a Networking Engineer 1. Strong Education Foundation The first step into your career as a networking engineer is formal education. A bachelor's degree in fields like Computer Science, Information Technology, or Electronics and Communication Engineering can be highly recommended. However, some professionals initiate their journey with diploma programs or associate degrees in networking and related fields. - BCA degree that teaches students all about courses on networking, cybersecurity, cloud computing, and much more. - B.Tech or B.Sc in IT/Computer Science: These are courses that provide technical know-how relevant to networking roles. While it is not always a requirement to have a degree, definitely, this is the doorway to better job opportunities and a foundation for needed technical skills. Also read: How to Choose the Right BCA Program for Your Career? 2. Practical Experience No theory can make you a brilliant networking engineer unless you have experience practicing. Gain hands-on skills in the following: configuration and network troubleshooting. You can do this by: - Apply for internships with IT firms, telecommunication companies, or large enterprises. Work towards maintaining their networks. Practical experience will increase your confidence and your technical capabilities. - Home Labs Using tools such as Cisco Packet Tracer or GNS3, you will get to set up your home network lab with all abilities to real simulate real-world networking environments. - Practicals are a must as network engineers have to deal with intricate networks and troubleshoot issues in real-time. 3. Obtain Networking Certifications Networking certifications are important as they would prove your capability and give assurance to the employer about your skills. Currently, for a networking engineer in 2024, the most widely sought-after certifications include the following: - Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA): It is one of the most popular entry certifications that cover networking basics and would help act as a stepping stone for further degrees. - CompTIA Network+: Focuses on understanding of concepts in networking, troubleshooting, and basic security practices. - CCNP: Once you have mastered the basics, then this professional certification will boost your career into mastering the complex topics of more serious networking issues. - CISSP: With more and more cybersecurity considerations becoming important, it will add security expertise to your networking skills. These certifications are offered by organizations that are truly legitimate in the industry, such as Cisco, CompTIA, and Juniper Networks. Apart from making a person stand out against fellow applicants for a job, it also affects the actual salary that one will receive. 4. Train Soft Skills In addition to technical knowledge, today's networking engineer must possess some good soft skills too: - Problem-solving: Networks always seem to face problems at times, and you have to be equipped with the skills to identify and troubleshoot issues quickly. - Communication: It often involves task description of technical issues to team members who are not well versed in technology, thus, good communication is vital. - Teamwork: Networking engineers work in teams with developers, administrators, and IT managers, so teamwork is very helpful. These skills make for a balanced candidate who may not only heed the job technically but also be able to deal with the interpersonal requirements of the job. 5. Explore Advanced Networking Technologies The space of networking is dynamic and keeps on changing every time. For 2024, the focus areas of the industry are cloud computing, 5G, SDN (Software Defined Networking), and network automation. Keeping tabs on these technologies will prepare an individual for today's job market. - Cloud Networking: More infrastructure will be migrated to the cloud with the passage of time; there is a need in the field of networking engineering that know cloud platforms such as AWS and Microsoft Azure. - 5G Technology: Networking engineers must have a good understanding of 5G and its applicability to enterprise networks as well as to existing wireless technologies. - Network Automation: The use of ANSIBLE and Python scripting has evolved to be fundamental while managing networks at a large scale. Acquiring this advanced technology enables the opportunity of specialization within those fields of work and, thus, getting well-paying jobs. Conclusion Being a networking engineer in 2024 is not just exciting but also challenging. It requires a solid educational background, practical experience, essential certifications, and the ability to adapt to emerging technologies like cloud computing and 5G. At Jetking, we guide you every step of the way. Our BCA in Cloud Computing and Cybersecurity is a 3-year UGC-approved degree program designed to provide you with the skills needed for a successful career in networking engineering. Whether you’re starting from scratch or looking to upskill, our industry-recognized programs offer hands-on training that sets you apart in the competitive job market.
